text:
Anya: Heads-up — noticed SLO burn spikes in eu-west this morning that align with cluster autoscaler churn. Looks like we’re treating transient provisioning latency as real availability violations.

Mike: Can you paste the panel/grafana link? I want to see the timing vs scale-up events.

Anya: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/serving/slo-overview?orgId=1&view=eu-west — zoom to 06:10–06:30. You can see p95 latency jump and error budget burn, but node provisioning events start ~06:12 and finish ~06:18.

Sam: This has bitten us before — alerts fire on 5m burn windows and make Pager noise while autoscaler is doing its thing. We should split SLOs so "availability" excludes short provisioning windows or have a separate "capacity-saturation" SLI.

Leon: +1. Proposal: keep current uptime SLO for customer-facing endpoints, but introduce a distinct saturation SLI/tagged by `gpu_type` and `shard` for capacity-induced failures. That way we can have different alert thresholds and runbooks.

Anya: Draft Prometheus recording rules I tested locally:

```
# record errors per shard for 1h windows
- record: infra:request_errors:rate1h
  expr: increase(serving_request_errors_total{job="runtime"}[1h])

# normalized error rate per shard
- record: infra:request_error_rate:1h
  expr: infra:request_errors:rate1h / ignoring(instance) group_left sum by (shard) (increase(serving_requests_total{job="runtime"}[1h]))
```

Sam: Hmm prefer using `sum_over_time` for clarity on long windows, but `increase()` is fine if counters are reset-safe. We should also include labels: `customer_tier`, `gpu_family`.

Mike: For burn-rate alerts we should smooth short spikes. My suggestion: compute a 1h burn rate and alert only if burn_rate > 0.01 for 30m AND cumulative budget consumption > X. Example PromQL sketch: 

```
# 1h error rate per shard
burn_1h = sum(increase(serving_bad_responses_total[1h])) by (shard) / sum(increase(serving_requests_total[1h])) by (shard)
# alert if sustained
burn_1h > 0.01
```

Jess: We also need to suppress alerts while autoscaler is in-flight. infra-bot already emits `cluster_autoscaler_event{shard="...",phase="scaling"}`. We can add a `for` clause or use `unless` with a recent() check.

Anya: Example alert rule I prototype:

```
alert: SustainedHighBurnByShard
expr: (sum(increase(serving_bad_responses_total[1h])) by (shard) / sum(increase(serving_requests_total[1h])) by (shard)) > 0.015
  unless sum_over_time(cluster_autoscaler_event{phase="scaling"}[30m]) > 0
for: 30m
labels:
  severity: page
annotations:
  summary: "Sustained high error burn in shard {{ $labels.shard }}"
  runbook: "https://wiki.redwood.internal/runbooks/slo#capacity-vs-availability"
```

Leon: Nice. Also include `gpu_family` and `customer_tier` in the alert labels so OnCall has context on whether this impacts premium customers.

Sam: Operational changes:
- Create a Grafana folder `SRE / SLOs / capacity` and move capacity-focused panels there.
- Add a composite dashboard that overlays autoscaler events and pod/node lifecycle graphs with the error burnrate.
- Update runbook to instruct on when to escalate to infra (vs. when to let autoscaler finish).

Anya: Small tweak: use EWM smoothing for UI panels to make spikes less noisy but keep raw metrics export for alerts. Example: Grafana transform `Exponential moving average` w/ span=5.

Mike: Question: do we want to adjust the uptime SLO objective to be more forgiving for short provisioning? Legal/reg teams may push back.

Jess: For Hosted customers with SLA add-on we need to be careful. We should keep SLA compliance calculation strict, but expose a separate operational SLO for internal paging. SLA reporting can still use the strict metric for billing.

Anya: TL;DR action items: 
- [Mike] Add `gpu_family` & `customer_tier` labels to recording rules (PR).
- [Sam] Create Grafana folder + composite dashboard (ticket: INF-4123).
- [Jess] Update alert rules to suppress when autoscaler events present; add labels for tier/family.
- [Leon] Draft runbook subsection for capacity vs availability and coordinate legal on SLA reporting.
- [Anya] Validate recording rules on canary cluster and roll to prod.

infra-bot: Created ticket INF-4123 and linked on the thread. :white_check_mark:

Mike: I'll pick up the recording rules PR today.

Sam: I'll start the Grafana folder template — want the panels to be shareable with Support.

Leon: Thanks all — this should cut a lot of unnecessary pages during normal scale events.

Jess: One more: add a Grafana alert mute when `customer_tier="internal"` to avoid noise from dev tenants.

Anya: Good call. I'll include that in the PR. :thumbsup:
